3	import '../../../../core/failure/failure.dart';
4	import '../entities/vault_status.dart';
5	
6	/// The epic's ONE new DI-singleton access point for device-level access
7	/// (AD-14) — `core/navigation/app_router.dart`'s `_redirect` reads
8	/// [currentStatus] before it reads `SessionRepository.currentStatus`
9	/// (Boundaries: "`_redirect` checks `VaultStatus` before `SessionStatus`").
10	/// Mirrors `features/auth/domain/repositories/session_repository.dart`'s
11	/// shape, except [currentStatus] is never nullable (see [VaultStatus]'s own
12	/// doc) and there is no `restoreSession`-equivalent boot call — the vault
13	/// is always [VaultStatus.locked] until a successful [authenticate] call.
14	abstract class VaultRepository {
15	  /// Broadcast stream of the current vault status. Unlike
16	  /// `SessionRepository.statusStream`, this always has a value from the
17	  /// moment the repository is constructed ([VaultStatus.locked]) — a late
18	  /// subscriber still immediately replays that cached value, same
19	  /// `Stream.multi` rationale as the session repository's own stream.
20	  Stream<VaultStatus> get statusStream;
21	
22	  /// The last status emitted on [statusStream], read synchronously —
23	  /// starts at [VaultStatus.locked] (never `null`, see [VaultStatus]'s own
24	  /// doc) and only a successful [authenticate] call ever flips it to
25	  /// [VaultStatus.unlocked].
26	  VaultStatus get currentStatus;
27	
28	  /// Triggers the OS biometric prompt (`local_auth`, `biometricOnly: true`
29	  /// — Boundaries: "never set `biometricOnly: false`"). Zero network calls
30	  /// (Boundaries: "Vault makes zero network calls"); never produces
31	  /// [Failure.authInvalid] (reserved for password login) — any failure here
32	  /// (OS declines, cancels, or throws `LocalAuthException`) maps to
33	  /// [Failure.malformedResponse] instead, and [currentStatus] stays
34	  /// [VaultStatus.locked]. Only a `true` result flips [currentStatus] to
35	  /// [VaultStatus.unlocked] and emits it on [statusStream].
36	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> authenticate();
37	
38	  /// Story 2.2's biometric-failure fallback. No PIN-creation screen exists
39	  /// anywhere in `docs/input/` (Design Notes): the first call ever made to
40	  /// this method — regardless of which screen reached the keypad — stores
41	  /// [pin] as the vault's PIN and immediately succeeds; every later call
42	  /// compares [pin] against that stored value. A match (first-use or
43	  /// later) flips [currentStatus] to [VaultStatus.unlocked] and emits it on
44	  /// [statusStream], same as a successful [authenticate]. A mismatch never
45	  /// throws, never caps retries, and leaves [currentStatus] at
46	  /// [VaultStatus.locked] — [Failure.malformedResponse] is returned instead
47	  /// (RNF09), so the caller always has a retryable path, never a dead end.
48	  Future<Either<Failure, Unit>> submitPin(String pin);
49	
50	  /// Releases the underlying stream resource. Wired as `get_it`'s
51	  /// `dispose:` callback on registration, so `resetCoreDependencies()`
52	  /// (`sl.reset()`) closes it instead of leaking a `StreamController` on
53	  /// every test teardown.
54	  Future<void> dispose();
55	}

7	/// The port later epics extend (Code Map) — `features/capture/` depends on
8	/// this abstract class only, never `entries/data` or `entries/presentation`
9	/// (RNF06).
10	abstract class EntriesRepository {
11	  /// Posts to `entries-create` (`ApiClient.post`, via
12	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`) and, on success, writes the entry through
13	  /// to the `entries` Hive box before returning `Right` (Boundaries) — a
14	  /// caller that only reads the returned [Entry] never needs to touch the
15	  /// box itself. Every [Failure] — including
16	  /// [Failure.networkOffline] — is returned as `Left`, unmapped and
17	  /// un-retried; the caller decides what to do with it (RNF09).
18	  ///
19	  /// spec-6-4 — [chatMessageId] is sent only when non-null (the pre-
20	  /// reserved `Entry.chatMessageId`/`EntrySource.chat` slot, Boundaries:
21	  /// "not a new architectural call"); every caller before RF10 passed
22	  /// `null` implicitly, so this is purely additive. Idempotent at the
23	  /// backend level for a given [chatMessageId] — a repeat call with the
24	  /// same value never creates a second Entry (epic context's own
25	  /// Technical Decisions).
26	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> create({
27	    required String content,
28	    required EntrySource source,
29	    int? mediaDurationSeconds,
30	    String? chatMessageId,
31	  });
32	
33	  /// Calls `entries-list` (`ApiClient.get`, via
34	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`), newest-first by `occurredAt` — server
35	  /// behavior assumed, undocumented (Code Map, decided per AGENTS.md
36	  /// policy: "where `docs/input/` is silent... decide and proceed").
37	  ///
38	  /// spec-5-2 — [source]/[dateFrom]/[dateTo] are forwarded to
39	  /// `entries-list` as its own `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` query
40	  /// parameters (`EntriesRemoteDataSource.list()`'s own doc), each only
41	  /// when non-null; combining more than one narrows with AND logic (the
42	  /// backend's own semantics, RF06 Acceptance Criteria) — this repository
43	  /// does no client-side filtering/joining of its own (AD-9).
44	  ///
45	  /// On [Failure.networkOffline]/[Failure.networkTimeout] specifically,
46	  /// falls back to a full dump of the `entries` Hive box, sorted
47	  /// `occurredAt` desc, with `EntriesPage.nextCursor: null` (Boundaries) —
48	  /// every *other* [Failure] (e.g. [Failure.authExpired]) propagates as
49	  /// `Left`, unmapped (RNF09). That fallback (`cursor == null` only) stays
50	  /// filter-oblivious regardless of [source]/[dateFrom]/[dateTo] — AD-9:
51	  /// the cache is never locally filtered, so an offline first page always
52	  /// renders the full cached list even with filters active.
53	  ///
54	  /// A successful page persists every item to the `entries` Hive box
55	  /// *before* returning `Right` — same "persist then return" ordering
56	  /// [create] already uses.
57	  Future<Either<Failure, EntriesPage>> list({
58	    String? cursor,
59	    int limit = 20,
60	    EntrySource? source,
61	    DateTime? dateFrom,
62	    DateTime? dateTo,
63	  });
64	
65	  /// spec-4-4 (RF07) — calls `entries-get` (`ApiClient.get`, via
66	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`) with [id] as the one path parameter, then
67	  /// persists the fetched entry to the `entries` Hive box (`put`) *before*
68	  /// returning `Right` — same "persist then return" ordering
69	  /// [create]/[list] already use. AD-11 keeps this port create+read-only,
70	  /// not count-capped — [search] (spec-5-1) added a fourth method without
71	  /// contradicting that.
72	  ///
73	  /// On [Failure.networkOffline]/[Failure.networkTimeout] specifically,
74	  /// falls back to `entriesBox.get(id)` if present; a cache miss propagates
75	  /// the original failure unchanged (no synthesized not-found — that
76	  /// distinction belongs to whichever `Failure` the backend/network
77	  /// actually produced). Every *other* [Failure] — including
78	  /// [Failure.notFound] for an id that never existed or belongs to another
79	  /// user — is returned as `Left`, unmapped (RNF09); RNF04 (identical
80	  /// treatment for both causes) is the caller's own rendering job, never
81	  /// this repository's.
82	  Future<Either<Failure, Entry>> getById(String id);
83	
84	  /// spec-5-1 — calls `entries-search` (`ApiClient.get`, via
85	  /// `EntriesRemoteDataSource`) with [query] as the one `q` query
86	  /// parameter (no `limit`/`cursor` — Boundaries). [query] is always
87	  /// already a non-empty, pre-trimmed string by the time it reaches this
88	  /// method — `EntriesSearchCubit` owns that guarantee, never this
89	  /// repository.
90	  ///
91	  /// spec-5-3 — [source]/[dateFrom]/[dateTo] are forwarded to
92	  /// `entries-search` as its own `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` query
93	  /// parameters, each only when non-null — same AND-narrowing convention
94	  /// [list]'s own doc already gives, now carried by `EntriesSearchCubit`'s
95	  /// own filter fields (`updateFilters()`) instead of `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s
96	  /// (the two cubits never share state directly, RNF06 — only
97	  /// `MeusRegistrosScreen` bridges them).
98	  ///
99	  /// On success, persists every returned entry to the `entries` Hive box
100	  /// (`putAll`) *before* returning `Right` — same "persist then return"
101	  /// ordering [list]/[getById] already use. Unlike [list]/[getById], there
102	  /// is no offline/timeout cache fallback here (AD-9: no client-side
103	  /// vector index) — every [Failure], including
104	  /// [Failure.networkOffline], is returned as `Left`, unmapped (RNF09).
105	  Future<Either<Failure, List<Entry>>> search(
106	    String query, {
107	    EntrySource? source,
108	    DateTime? dateFrom,
109	    DateTime? dateTo,
110	  });
111	}

9	/// The chat feature's one port — `features/chat/presentation` depends on
10	/// this abstract class only, never `chat/data` (RNF06). Every method but
11	/// [sendMessage] returns `Future<Either<Failure, T>>` (RNF09); [sendMessage]
12	/// alone returns a `Stream` given the SSE nature of its response
13	/// (Boundaries).
14	abstract class ChatRepository {
15	  /// Calls `chat-sessions-list` (`ApiClient.get`, via
16	  /// `ChatRemoteDataSource`) — works offline via the `chat_sessions` Hive
17	  /// box (Code Map): on [Failure.networkOffline]/[Failure.networkTimeout],
18	  /// falls back to a full dump of that box, same "cache fallback"
19	  /// convention `EntriesRepositoryImpl.list()` already uses for its own
20	  /// first/fresh page. Every other [Failure] propagates as `Left`,
21	  /// unmapped (RNF09).
22	  Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatSession>>> listSessions();
23	
24	  /// Calls `chat-sessions-create` (`ApiClient.post`) with no title
25	  /// (Boundaries: "`chat-sessions-create` with no title") — blocked
26	  /// offline per `requirements.md` ("`POST /chat/sessions` — blocked
27	  /// offline"), so unlike [listSessions] there is no cache fallback here:
28	  /// every [Failure], including [Failure.networkOffline], is returned as
29	  /// `Left`, unmapped. On success, persists the new session to the
30	  /// `chat_sessions` Hive box before returning `Right`, same
31	  /// "persist then return" ordering [listSessions] already uses.
32	  Future<Either<Failure, ChatSession>> createSession();
33	
34	  /// Calls `chat-messages-list` (`ApiClient.get`, [sessionId] appended as
35	  /// the one trailing path segment) — works offline via the
36	  /// `chat_messages` Hive box, same cache-fallback convention
37	  /// [listSessions] already uses, filtered to [sessionId] and sorted by
38	  /// `seq` ascending (the backend's own "ordered by seq", `openapi.yaml`).
39	  Future<Either<Failure, List<ChatMessage>>> listMessages(String sessionId);
40	
41	  /// Calls `chat-messages-send` (`ApiClient.postStream`, [sessionId]
42	  /// appended as the one trailing path segment) with `{content}` — the
43	  /// one streaming exception to this port's otherwise all-`Future` shape
44	  /// (Boundaries/RNF09: "every other method returns
45	  /// `Future<Either<Failure, T>>`"). No connectivity resolves immediately
46	  /// to a single `Left(Failure.networkOffline)` emission, never queued
47	  /// (Boundaries) — `ApiClient.postStream`'s own first awaited `Dio.post`
48	  /// call surfaces that failure before any byte streams. A connection that
49	  /// closes without a `done`/`error` SSE event is surfaced as a single
50	  /// trailing `Left(Failure.networkTimeout)` (Design Notes: "the taxonomy
51	  /// has no dedicated 'dropped stream' code"). No local write queue, no
52	  /// Hive persistence of sent messages (Design Notes: chat holds no local
53	  /// write queue for this story).
54	  Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>> sendMessage(
55	    String sessionId,
56	    String content,
57	  );
58	
59	  /// spec-6-3 — calls `chat-messages-retry` (`ApiClient.postStream`,
60	  /// [sessionId] then [userMessageId] appended as the two trailing path
61	  /// segments, `data: const {}`) — regenerates the AI response for an
62	  /// already-persisted user message without re-sending its content
63	  /// (Boundaries: "never a duplicate question"). Same streaming shape and
64	  /// terminal handling as [sendMessage] (SSE events via
65	  /// `ChatRemoteDataSource`'s shared buffer/parse helper); [userMessageId]
66	  /// must be a real, already-persisted user message id — `ChatCubit`
67	  /// itself never calls this with one that's `null` (Boundaries: "Never
68	  /// calling `chat-messages-retry` with no `serverId`"), falling back to
69	  /// [sendMessage] instead in that case.
70	  Stream<Either<Failure, ChatStreamEvent>> retryMessage(
71	    String sessionId,
72	    String userMessageId,
73	  );
74	
75	  /// spec-6-5 — calls `chat-insight-create` (`ApiClient.post`, [sessionId]
76	  /// appended as the one trailing path segment) with `{triggerType:
77	  /// triggerType.wireValue, triggerKey}`. `ChatCubit` fires this
78	  /// fire-and-forget, unawaited, through `isolatedSideEffect` — its first
79	  /// unawaited caller (Boundaries). `null` means "no insight to show": a
80	  /// successful (200) response whose `status` isn't `'ready'` — RF08:
81	  /// "never an HTTP error; a failure becomes status='failed'", so a
82	  /// genuine backend-side generation failure still arrives as a `Right`
83	  /// here, just carrying `null`. Only a transport-level problem (offline,
84	  /// timeout, malformed shape, etc.) surfaces as `Left`, unmapped
85	  /// (RNF09) — `ChatCubit` drops both cases silently either way
86	  /// (Boundaries).
87	  Future<Either<Failure, ChatInsight?>> generateInsight(
88	    String sessionId, {
89	    required InsightTriggerType triggerType,
90	    required String triggerKey,
91	  });
92	}

140	/// Calls [AccountSettingsRepository] directly (no use-case — same small-
141	/// scope rationale `AuthCubit`'s own doc gives). [toggleBiometric] is the
142	/// I/O matrix's optimistic flip/revert, end to end: the repository itself
143	/// flips [AccountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled] immediately
144	/// and emits it on [AccountSettingsRepository.biometricEnabledStream] —
145	/// this cubit only mirrors that stream into its own [AccountSettingsState]
146	/// (subscribed once, at construction) and separately layers the
147	/// toggle-failure error message on top.
148	class AccountSettingsCubit extends Cubit<AccountSettingsState> {
149	  AccountSettingsCubit(this._repository)
150	    : super(
151	        AccountSettingsState(
152	          biometricEnabled: _repository.currentBiometricEnabled,
153	          // spec-8-3 — read once, at construction (Boundaries); never
154	          // re-read from the repository afterwards.
155	          displayName: _repository.currentDisplayName,
156	          email: _repository.currentEmail,
157	        ),
158	      ) {
159	    _subscription = _repository.biometricEnabledStream.listen((value) {
160	      // Review finding: `biometricEnabledStream`'s first delivery always
161	      // replays the exact same value the constructor above just read
162	      // synchronously — without this check, that replay was a redundant
163	      // duplicate emission (not skipped by `Cubit`'s own equal-state dedup,
164	      // which only applies once something has already been emitted),
165	      // forcing one pointless extra rebuild right after every screen mount.
166	      if (value == state.biometricEnabled) {
167	        return;
168	      }
169	      emit(state.copyWith(biometricEnabled: value));
170	    });
171	  }
172	
173	  final AccountSettingsRepository _repository;
174	  late final StreamSubscription<bool> _subscription;
175	
176	  Future<void> toggleBiometric(bool value) async {
177	    emit(state.copyWith(clearErrorMessage: true, isSaving: true));
178	    final result = await _repository.setBiometricEnabled(value);
179	    // Review finding: this cubit is a `get_it` lazy singleton with
180	    // `dispose: (cubit) => cubit.close()` — if `close()` runs while the
181	    // `await` above is still pending (e.g. `resetCoreDependencies()`
182	    // during a logout, once Epic 8 implements one), `emit()` below would
183	    // otherwise throw a `StateError` ("Cannot emit new states after
184	    // calling close"), unlike the repository-layer `_emit` methods in this
185	    // codebase, which already guard against the equivalent race.
186	    if (isClosed) {
187	      return;
188	    }
189	    result.match((failure) {
190	      // Review finding: a superseded call's `Left` is an internal
191	      // control-flow signal (`AccountSettingsRepository.
192	      // supersededMessage`), not a real error — the winning call already
193	      // settled the value correctly, so nothing should be shown; showing
194	      // `failure.message` unconditionally leaked that raw, English,
195	      // internal string into this otherwise fully Portuguese screen.
196	      if (failure.message == AccountSettingsRepository.supersededMessage) {
197	        emit(state.copyWith(isSaving: false));
198	        return;
199	      }
200	      emit(state.copyWith(errorMessage: failure.message, isSaving: false));
201	    }, (_) => emit(state.copyWith(isSaving: false)));
202	  }
203	
204	  /// Review finding: [errorMessage] previously cleared only at the start of
205	  /// the *next* [toggleBiometric] call — since this cubit is a DI
206	  /// singleton that outlives any single Configurações visit, a failed
207	  /// toggle's error text would otherwise still be showing if the user
208	  /// left the screen and came back later with no new attempt made.
209	  /// `account_settings_screen.dart` calls this once, on mount, same
210	  /// "stale message must not linger unchanged" fix already applied to
211	  /// `vault_lock_screen.dart`'s own PIN-mismatch error, just anchored to
212	  /// screen-entry instead of attempt-start.
213	  void clearStaleError() {
214	    if (state.errorMessage != null) {
215	      emit(state.copyWith(clearErrorMessage: true));
216	    }
217	  }
218	
219	  /// spec-8-3 — tapping the pencil icon (I/O matrix: "Tap pencil ->
220	  /// `isEditingName: false` -> Field replaces name, draft = current, icon
221	  /// -> check"). Also clears any leftover [AccountSettingsState.
222	  /// nameErrorMessage] from a previous failed attempt.
223	  void startEditingName() {
224	    emit(
225	      state.copyWith(
226	        isEditingName: true,
227	        nameDraft: state.displayName,
228	        clearNameErrorMessage: true,
229	      ),
230	    );
231	  }
232	
233	  /// spec-8-3 — mirrors the field's own `onChanged`, kept as the single
234	  /// source [confirmEditingName] reads from.
235	  void updateNameDraft(String value) {
236	    emit(state.copyWith(nameDraft: value));
237	  }
238	
239	  /// spec-8-3 — I/O matrix: "Tap away, not saving -> Reverts, draft
240	  /// discarded, no PATCH" / "Tap away, saving -> No-op, save completes".
241	  /// A no-op while [AccountSettingsState.isSavingName] (Boundaries) — the
242	  /// in-flight [confirmEditingName] call owns the eventual transition back
243	  /// to display mode.
244	  void cancelEditingName() {
245	    if (state.isSavingName) {
246	      return;
247	    }
248	    emit(state.copyWith(isEditingName: false, clearNameErrorMessage: true));
249	  }
250	
251	  /// spec-8-3 — tapping the check icon. Trims [AccountSettingsState.
252	  /// nameDraft] only for the empty/unchanged comparison and the PATCH
253	  /// payload itself; an empty or unchanged draft reverts immediately with
254	  /// no PATCH (I/O matrix). Otherwise awaits
255	  /// `AccountSettingsRepository.setDisplayName` (not optimistic,
256	  /// Boundaries) — success reverts to display mode showing the new name;
257	  /// failure stays in edit mode with the draft kept and an inline error.
258	  Future<void> confirmEditingName() async {
259	    final trimmed = state.nameDraft.trim();
260	    if (trimmed.isEmpty || trimmed == state.displayName) {
261	      emit(state.copyWith(isEditingName: false, clearNameErrorMessage: true));
262	      return;
263	    }
264	    emit(state.copyWith(isSavingName: true, clearNameErrorMessage: true));
265	    final result = await _repository.setDisplayName(trimmed);
266	    // Same close()-race guard as toggleBiometric's own.
267	    if (isClosed) {
268	      return;
269	    }
270	    result.match(
271	      (failure) {
272	        // Same superseded-message filtering convention as toggleBiometric's
273	        // own failure branch — an internal control-flow signal, not a real
274	        // error to show.
275	        if (failure.message == AccountSettingsRepository.supersededMessage) {
276	          emit(state.copyWith(isSavingName: false));
277	          return;
278	        }
279	        emit(
280	          state.copyWith(
281	            isSavingName: false,
282	            nameErrorMessage: failure.message,
283	          ),
284	        );
285	      },
286	      (_) {
287	        // Review finding: reads the repository's own echoed value (set
288	        // from `dto.displayName` in `setDisplayName`'s success branch),
289	        // not the locally-sent `trimmed` string — any backend-side
290	        // normalization (trimming, casing, etc.) must reach this state,
291	        // the one place the user actually sees the name, not just the
292	        // repository's own internal cache.
293	        emit(
294	          state.copyWith(
295	            isEditingName: false,
296	            isSavingName: false,
297	            displayName: _repository.currentDisplayName,
298	            clearNameErrorMessage: true,
299	          ),
300	        );
301	      },
302	    );
303	  }
304	
305	  @override
306	  Future<void> close() async {
307	    await _subscription.cancel();
308	    return super.close();
309	  }
310	}

94	  /// first letter of the first word plus first letter of the last word (a

98	  /// Code-review patch: extracts each initial via `Characters.first`
99	  /// (Unicode grapheme-cluster aware), not `String.substring(0, 1)` —
100	  /// `substring` slices by UTF-16 code unit, which would split an astral-
101	  /// plane character (e.g. an emoji) that starts a word into an unpaired
102	  /// surrogate half.
103	  String _initialsFor(String name) {
104	    final words = name
105	        .trim()

107	        .where((w) => w.isNotEmpty)

109	    if (words.isEmpty) {
110	      return '';

113	    if (words.length == 1) {

115	    }
116	    final last = words.last.characters.first;
117	    return '$first$last';

7	/// Registers the `account` feature into the project's single `get_it`
8	/// instance (`sl`) — mirrors `features/vault/vault_injection.dart`'s
9	/// pattern. Called from `setupCoreDependencies()` right after
10	/// `registerVaultFeature()` (Code Map).
11	void registerAccountFeature() {
12	  sl.registerLazySingleton<AccountRemoteDataSource>(
13	    () => AccountRemoteDataSource(sl()),
14	  );
15	
16	  // The epic's one new DI-singleton access point for the account's
17	  // `biometricEnabled` preference — registered as a singleton so every
18	  // consumer (`main.dart`'s boot fetch; `core/navigation/app_router.dart`'s
19	  // `/vault` builder; the Configurações screen's own cubit) shares the same
20	  // `biometricEnabledStream`, not a fresh instance each. `dispose:` wires
21	  // `AccountSettingsRepository.dispose()` into `get_it`'s own reset
22	  // lifecycle, so `resetCoreDependencies()` (`sl.reset()`) closes its
23	  // `StreamController` instead of leaking one on every test teardown.
24	  sl.registerLazySingleton<AccountSettingsRepository>(
25	    () => AccountSettingsRepositoryImpl(remoteDataSource: sl()),
26	    dispose: (repository) => repository.dispose(),
27	  );
28	
29	  // Review finding: `AccountSettingsCubit`'s constructor subscribes to
30	  // `biometricEnabledStream`; only its own `close()` cancels that
31	  // subscription, which nothing previously called — `dispose:` wires it
32	  // into `get_it`'s own reset lifecycle, same convention as every other
33	  // registration in this file.
34	  sl.registerLazySingleton<AccountSettingsCubit>(
35	    () => AccountSettingsCubit(sl()),
36	    dispose: (cubit) => cubit.close(),
37	  );
38	}

31	/// The epic's ONE `GoRouter`/`redirect` (Boundaries: "never a second
32	/// competing `redirect`") — composes [VaultRepository.currentStatus] first,
33	/// then [SessionRepository.currentStatus] (AD-14). All three repositories
34	/// are taken as parameters (rather than this file reaching into `sl`
35	/// itself) purely so a test can pass fakes/mocks directly, without
36	/// touching the global DI container; `AccountSettingsRepository` (Story
37	/// 2.4) plays no part in `_redirect` and needs no `refreshListenable` entry
38	/// of its own — `currentBiometricEnabled` is read synchronously at
39	/// `/vault`'s own build time below, same convention `_redirect` already
40	/// uses for `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus`, so every fresh navigation into
41	/// `/vault` (triggered by those two streams, as already happens today)
42	/// already picks up the latest value correctly. (Review finding: a
43	/// `biometricEnabledStream` entry was tried here to also cover a value
44	/// changing while already resident at `/vault`, but go_router 18.1.1's
45	/// `GoRouterDelegate.setNewRoutePath` short-circuits whenever the matched
46	/// `RouteMatchList` is unchanged — which it always is here, since
47	/// `_redirect` stays at `/vault` before and after — so the route's
48	/// `builder` is never actually re-invoked that way; removed as dead code
49	/// rather than kept as a misleading no-op. That's a one-time, benign gap —
50	/// at most one extra biometric prompt on a slow-network cold boot, never a
51	/// security or dead-end issue, since PIN fallback is untouched and there's
52	/// no way to interrupt an in-flight native biometric dialog regardless —
53	/// which the frozen spec's I/O matrix never promised to cover.
54	/// `VaultLockScreen.didUpdateWidget` still defensively honors a changed
55	/// `attemptBiometricFirst` if the widget is ever rebuilt by some other
56	/// means.) The Configurações screen gets its own reactivity to this value
57	/// directly from `AccountSettingsCubit`'s independent subscription to
58	/// `biometricEnabledStream` — unrelated to routing.
59	///
60	/// [navigatorKey] is accepted explicitly (rather than letting `GoRouter`
61	/// generate its own internally) so the caller — `main.dart`'s
62	/// `ExpiryOverlayHost` — can reach the Navigator's own `BuildContext`
63	/// through the same, public, documented key instead of reaching into
64	/// `GoRouter`'s internal `routerDelegate` (not part of its public API).
65	GoRouter buildAppRouter({
66	  required VaultRepository vaultRepository,
67	  required SessionRepository sessionRepository,
68	  required AccountSettingsRepository accountSettingsRepository,
69	  required GlobalKey<NavigatorState> navigatorKey,
70	}) {
71	  return GoRouter(
72	    navigatorKey: navigatorKey,
73	    initialLocation: AppRoutePaths.boot,
74	    refreshListenable: _GoRouterRefreshStream([
75	      vaultRepository.statusStream,
76	      sessionRepository.statusStream,
77	    ]),
78	    redirect: (context, state) =>
79	        _redirect(vaultRepository, sessionRepository, state),
80	    routes: [
81	      GoRoute(
82	        path: AppRoutePaths.vaultLock,
83	        builder: (context, state) => VaultLockScreen(
84	          vaultRepository: vaultRepository,
85	          // Story 2.4 — read synchronously, same sync-getter convention
86	          // `_redirect` already uses for `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus`
87	          // below: `true` (the default before the boot fetch resolves)
88	          // attempts biometric first, `false` skips straight to the PIN
89	          // keypad (Boundaries).
90	          attemptBiometricFirst:
91	              accountSettingsRepository.currentBiometricEnabled,
92	        ),
93	      ),
94	      GoRoute(
95	        path: AppRoutePaths.boot,
96	        builder: (context, state) => const BootSplashScreen(),
97	      ),
98	      GoRoute(
99	        path: AppRoutePaths.auth,
100	        builder: (context, state) => AuthScreen(
101	          cubit: sl<AuthCubit>(),
102	          onAuthenticated: (context) => context.go(AppRoutePaths.home),
103	        ),
104	      ),
105	      GoRoute(
106	        path: AppRoutePaths.reauth,
107	        builder: (context, state) => const BiometricReauthPlaceholderScreen(),
108	      ),
109	      GoRoute(
110	        path: AppRoutePaths.home,
111	        builder: (context, state) => ChatScreen(cubit: sl<ChatCubit>()),
112	      ),
113	      GoRoute(
114	        path: AppRoutePaths.meusRegistros,
115	        builder: (context, state) => MeusRegistrosScreen(
116	          cubit: sl<MeusRegistrosCubit>(),
117	          searchCubit: sl<EntriesSearchCubit>(),
118	        ),
119	        routes: [
120	          // spec-4-4 (RF07) — `:id` is either a real server id or a
121	          // still-pending/failed placeholder's synthetic `tempId`
122	          // (Boundaries: "a valid, un-special-cased navigation target");
123	          // `EntryDetailCubit` itself decides nothing about which kind it
124	          // is, it just calls `getById` with it verbatim.
125	          GoRoute(
126	            path: ':id',
127	            builder: (context, state) => EntryDetailScreen(
128	              cubit: sl<EntryDetailCubit>()..load(state.pathParameters['id']!),
129	            ),
130	          ),
131	        ],
132	      ),

136	      ),

143	        ),

149	/// I/O & Edge-Case Matrix:
150	/// - status not yet known (`null`) -> `/boot`, unless already there.
151	/// - `unauthenticated` -> `/auth`, unless already there.
152	/// - `authenticated`/`expired` -> leaves `/boot`/`/auth` for `/`; every
153	///   other location is left alone *except* `/reauth` while already
154	///   `authenticated` (bounced home below — `/reauth` is meant to be
155	///   reached only by the expiry overlay's own explicit navigation while
156	///   `expired`, code review Story 1.6) — a mid-session expiry never
157	///   navigates away (Story 1.5 behavior preserved), and the three
158	///   non-Home destinations stay reachable while `expired`.
159	///
160	/// AD-14: Epic 2's `VaultStatus` gate (RF03) is composed first, strictly
161	/// ahead of every `SessionStatus` check below — the vault gate overrides
162	/// any location whenever it isn't `unlocked`, and only once it is does the
163	/// rest of this function (unchanged from Story 1.6) ever run.
164	String? _redirect(
165	  VaultRepository vaultRepository,
166	  SessionRepository sessionRepository,
167	  GoRouterState state,
168	) {
169	  final location = state.matchedLocation;
170	
171	  // AD-14 — checked before SessionStatus, per Boundaries ("`_redirect`
172	  // checks `VaultStatus` before `SessionStatus`"). `VaultStatus.locked` is
173	  // the default from construction (never `null`), so this never waits on
174	  // an async warm-up the way the `status == null` boot check below does.
175	  if (vaultRepository.currentStatus != VaultStatus.unlocked) {
176	    return location == AppRoutePaths.vaultLock ? null : AppRoutePaths.vaultLock;
177	  }
178	
179	  final status = sessionRepository.currentStatus;
180	
181	  if (status == null) {
182	    return location == AppRoutePaths.boot ? null : AppRoutePaths.boot;
183	  }
184	
185	  if (status == SessionStatus.unauthenticated) {
186	    return location == AppRoutePaths.auth ? null : AppRoutePaths.auth;
187	  }
188	
189	  // status is authenticated or expired.
190	  // `vaultLock` is included here too: once the vault unlocks while this
191	  // location is still `/vault` (the normal cold-start path once
192	  // `authenticate()` succeeds), the same fall-through that already bounces
193	  // `/boot`/`/auth` to Home applies — `/vault` is never a valid resting
194	  // place once `VaultStatus.unlocked`.
195	  if (location == AppRoutePaths.boot ||
196	      location == AppRoutePaths.auth ||
197	      location == AppRoutePaths.vaultLock) {
198	    return AppRoutePaths.home;
199	  }
200	  // `/reauth` is a throwaway placeholder standing in for Epic 2's real
201	  // reauth flow; it should never be sitting open once the session is back
202	  // to fully `authenticated` (code review, Story 1.6).
203	  if (location == AppRoutePaths.reauth &&
204	      status == SessionStatus.authenticated) {
205	    return AppRoutePaths.home;
206	  }
207	  return null;
208	}
209	
210	/// Wraps [streams] as a single `Listenable` so `GoRouter`'s
211	/// `refreshListenable` can re-run [_redirect] on every emission from either
212	/// one — go_router 18.1.1 exports no `GoRouterRefreshStream` of its own
213	/// (Code Map), so this is that small local class. Extended by AD-14 to
214	/// subscribe to both the vault and the session streams (previously just
215	/// the one session stream), composing them into the one `Listenable`
216	/// `GoRouter` itself requires (Boundaries: "never a second
217	/// `GoRouter`/`redirect`").
218	class _GoRouterRefreshStream extends ChangeNotifier {
219	  _GoRouterRefreshStream(Iterable<Stream<dynamic>> streams) {
220	    _subscriptions = [
221	      for (final stream in streams)
222	        stream.listen(
223	          (_) => notifyListeners(),
224	          // Mirrors `ExpiryOverlayHost`'s and `SessionRepositoryImpl`'s own
225	          // subscriptions to this same stream — no current implementation
226	          // ever errors on it, but a future one that did must not surface
227	          // as an unhandled zone exception here specifically.
228	          onError: (_, _) {},
229	        ),
230	    ];
231	  }
232	
233	  late final List<StreamSubscription<dynamic>> _subscriptions;
234	
235	  @override
236	  void dispose() {
237	    for (final subscription in _subscriptions) {
238	      subscription.cancel();
239	    }
240	    super.dispose();
241	  }
242	}

# Cerne backend — documentation package

The backend is already built and frozen. This package documents what the app needs to consume it. The backend source code is not part of it.

## Contents

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `api/openapi.yaml` | API contract of the 23 endpoints — the source of truth |
| `error-taxonomy.md` | The 13 error codes, with HTTP status and `retryable` |
| `export-screen-states.md` | Mapping between the export screen states and the export job statuses (RF05) |
| `sync-badge.md` | Semantics of the per-entry synchronization badge |
| `known-bugs.md` | Known non-blocking backend defects, with workarounds |
| `fixtures/` | Test media (audio, images for OCR), the expected transcription of the audio, and the three seeded entries used by semantic search |

Credentials (project URL and keys) are not in this package: they are provided in the app's `.env`.

## Contract path → function

`api/openapi.yaml` has no router: each operation is served by its own Edge Function at `{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>` (see `servers` and each operation's `x-cerne-function` in the YAML) — **never** directly at the REST path below. Path parameters are appended as the final URL segments, in the same order as they appear in the path; any literal segment after the last parameter (e.g., the `/retry` of `chat.messages.retry`) does not exist in the real URL.

| Contract path | Function (`{FUNCTIONS_BASE_URL}/<function>`) |
|---|---|
| `POST /auth/signup` | `auth-signup` |
| `POST /auth/login` | `auth-login` |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | `auth-refresh` |
| `GET /auth/session` | `auth-session` |
| `POST /auth/logout` | `auth-logout` |
| `POST /entries` | `entries-create` |
| `GET /entries` | `entries-list` |
| `GET /entries/{id}` | `entries-get` |
| `GET /entries/search` | `entries-search` |
| `POST /media/ocr` | `media-ocr` |
| `POST /chat/sessions` | `chat-sessions-create` |
| `GET /chat/sessions` | `chat-sessions-list` |
| `GET /chat/sessions/{id}/messages` | `chat-messages-list` |
| `POST /chat/sessions/{id}/messages` | `chat-messages-send` |
| `POST /chat/sessions/{id}/messages/{userMessageId}/retry` | `chat-messages-retry` |
| `POST /chat/sessions/{id}/insight` | `chat-insight-create` |
| `POST /export/summary` | `export-summary-create` |

**1. `lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart`** — `clearLocalCache()` now clears `_sessionsBox` and `_messagesBox` in two independent try/catch blocks (tracking `firstError`) instead of one shared try/catch, so a throw on the first box no longer skips the second. **2. `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart`** — `logout()` now captures `Future.wait([...])`'s results and `debugPrint`s a message for any `Left` (entries/chat cache-clear failure), matching the existing silent-swallow-with-debugPrint convention (`ApiClient.postStream`/`HeaderInterceptor`). input.message:
Applied all 4 review-patch fixes for spec-8-4-logout.md in this same session, then re-ran the spec's Verification commands. Both are clean.

## What changed

**1. `lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart`** — `clearLocalCache()` previously awaited `_sessionsBox.clear()` then `_messagesBox.clear()` inside one shared try/catch, so a throw on the first box skipped the second entirely. Rewrote it to clear both boxes independently (separate try/catch each, tracking `firstError`) — both are now always attempted; returns `Left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))` if either failed, `Right(unit)` only if both succeeded. Added two new tests in `test/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl_test.dart` proving the second box is still attempted when the first throws, and vice versa.

**2. `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart`** — `logout()`'s `await Future.wait([...])` result was never inspected. Now captures the results and `debugPrint`s a message for any `Left` from either `clearLocalCache()` call, matching this codebase's existing silent-swallow-with-debugPrint convention (`ApiClient.postStream`/`HeaderInterceptor`). Added `import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';`. Still never surfaces anything to the UI — the "no backend-logout-failure error" boundary is untouched.

**3. `test/features/auth/data/datasources/auth_remote_data_source_test.dart`** — added a new `AuthRemoteDataSource.logout` group (mirroring the existing `refresh()` test pattern): verifies `ApiClient.post` is called with exactly `'auth-logout'` and no body, that a successful response maps to `Right(unit)`, and that a `Left` from `ApiClient.post` propagates unchanged through `.map((_) => unit)`.

**4. `test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen_test.dart`** — the "tapping Sair" test only asserted fake call-counts, never that the router redirected. Split the old `pumpWithLogoutFakes` helper into two: the original (plain, non-navigating two-route stub) stays for the two tests that need the screen to remain mounted through the assertion (button renders; button disables while in flight — a real redirect would unmount the screen mid-test for those), and a new `pumpWithLogoutFakesAndVaultGate` builds a dedicated router with a real AD-14-style vault gate (`redirect` + a new `_StreamRefreshListenable` on the fake `VaultRepository`'s stream) used only by the "tapping Sair" test, which now asserts `router.state.uri.toString() == AppRoutePaths.vaultLock` after the tap. Had to make `_FakeVaultRepository.currentStatus`/`statusStream` in this file stateful (previously `throw UnimplementedError`) so the gate could observe real lock state — this exposed and required fixing a real coupling: with the gate wired in, the pre-existing double-tap test started failing ("No element" — the screen had already navigated away) until I confirmed it should use the plain, non-gated router instead, since that test's job is the button's own disabled state, not navigation.

## What changed

**1. `lib/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl.dart`** — `clearLocalCache()` previously awaited `_sessionsBox.clear()` then `_messagesBox.clear()` inside one shared try/catch, so a throw on the first box skipped the second entirely. Rewrote it to clear both boxes independently (separate try/catch each, tracking `firstError`) — both are now always attempted; returns `Left(Failure.malformedResponse(...))` if either failed, `Right(unit)` only if both succeeded. Added two new tests in `test/features/chat/data/repositories/chat_repository_impl_test.dart` proving the second box is still attempted when the first throws, and vice versa.

**2. `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart`** — `logout()`'s `await Future.wait([...])` result was never inspected. Now captures the results and `debugPrint`s a message for any `Left` from either `clearLocalCache()` call, matching this codebase's existing silent-swallow-with-debugPrint convention (`ApiClient.postStream`/`HeaderInterceptor`). Added `import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';`. Still never surfaces anything to the UI — the "no backend-logout-failure error" boundary is untouched.

**3. `test/features/auth/data/datasources/auth_remote_data_source_test.dart`** — added a new `AuthRemoteDataSource.logout` group (mirroring the existing `refresh()` test pattern): verifies `ApiClient.post` is called with exactly `'auth-logout'` and no body, that a successful response maps to `Right(unit)`, and that a `Left` from `ApiClient.post` propagates unchanged through `.map((_) => unit)`.

**4. `test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen_test.dart`** — the "tapping Sair" test only asserted fake call-counts, never that the router redirected. Split the old `pumpWithLogoutFakes` helper into two: the original (plain, non-navigating two-route stub) stays for the two tests that need the screen to remain mounted through the assertion (button renders; button disables while in flight — a real redirect would unmount the screen mid-test for those), and a new `pumpWithLogoutFakesAndVaultGate` builds a dedicated router with a real AD-14-style vault gate (`redirect` + a new `_StreamRefreshListenable` on the fake `VaultRepository`'s stream) used only by the "tapping Sair" test, which now asserts `router.state.uri.toString() == AppRoutePaths.vaultLock` after the tap.
